summary: The cardholder starts the billing cycle with no previous balance, makes purchases that push the account above its credit limit, and reaches statement closing while still over limit. The scenario is designed to exercise the over-limit-at-statement-close condition while also showing that the grace-period narrative exists but the payment obligation remains unmet because the due date falls after the statement close.
assumptions: The account begins a new billing cycle with no previous balance, so the grace-period condition for new purchases is satisfied under clause-6-grace-period.
The issuer allows the purchases to post even though the resulting outstanding balance exceeds the stated credit limit, so the account can be over limit at statement close.
No payments are made before the statement close, so the full posted purchase balance remains outstanding on the statement date.
The payment due date for the statement occurs after the statement_close event, so the minimum payment obligation is included for traceability but is not yet performed within this scenario timeline.

Any over-limit fee that may be assessed by the issuer is outside the bound obligation list supplied for event binding, so this scenario focuses on the factual over-limit condition at statement close rather than modeling a separate fee event.
